Then $0 \le I_m[\mu]$, and moreover $I_m[\mu]=0$ if and only if for every $p=(p_1,p_2)\in S	imes U$, $\mu(\{p\}) = ((\pi_1)_*\mu)(\{p_1\})\cdot((\pi_2)_*\mu)(\{p_2\})$, all measures of singletons being taken as real numbers. Here, for a measure $
u$ on a measurable space $Y$, $H_m[
u] \in \mathbb{R}$ denotes the measure entropy `measureEntropy ν`, defined as $H_m[
u] = \sum_{y \in Y} \mathrm{negMulLog} ig(	ilde
u(\{y\}) ig)$ (an unconditional sum `tsum` of reals), where $	ilde
u = (
u(Y))^{-1}\,
u$ is $
u$ rescaled by the inverse of its total mass (inverse taken in $[0,\infty]$), $	ilde
u(\{y\})$ is taken as a real number (`Measure.real`), and $\mathrm{negMulLog}(x) = -x \log x$. For measurable spaces $S$, $U$ and a measure $ho$ on $S 	imes U$, $I_m[ho] \in \mathbb{R}$ denotes the mutual information `measureMutualInfo ρ` between the marginals of $ho$, defined as $I_m[ho] = H_m[(\pi_1)_*ho] + H_m[(\pi_2)_*ho] - H_m[ho]$, where $\pi_1 : S 	imes U 	o S$ and $\pi_2 : S 	imes U 	o U$ are the coordinate projections and $(\pi_i)_*$ denotes the pushforward (`Measure.map`).
